# Research earthquake catalogues on Zenodo (one CSV per record)

`zenodo_catalog` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `seismic_catalog` tokens

| | |
|---|---|
| Provider | The authors the region names (Tan et al., Fonzetti et al., Poggiali et al.) |
| Home | https://zenodo.org |
| Licence | `LicenseRef-per-region` |

## Terms

Each region's YAML names the record, its authors, licence and citation; the three catalogues of P8c are CC BY 4.0. Cite the catalogue and its paper.

## Cite

- Tan, Y. J., Waldhauser, F., Ellsworth, W. L., et al. (2021). Machine-Learning-Based High-Resolution Earthquake Catalog Reveals How Complex Fault Structures Were Activated during the 2016-2017 Central Italy Sequence. The Seismic Record 1(1), 11-19. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4736089
- Fonzetti, R., Govoni, A., De Gori, P., Valoroso, L., Chiarabba, C. (2025). Machine learning-based high-resolution data set for the 2009 L'Aquila earthquake sequence. Geophysical Journal International. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16535092
- Poggiali, G., et al. (2025). Fault Geometry and Source Mechanics of the Altotiberina Fault System from a High-Resolution Machine-Learning Earthquake Catalog. Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America 115(5), 2181-2201. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15622508

## Access

One CSV per record through Zenodo's files API, checked against the record's MD5, downloaded once and cached by hash.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `event` |
| `lat, lon, depth_km` | the columns the region names |
| `time` | one ISO 8601 column (UTC) or year … second columns |
| `value` | the magnitude column the region names |
| `qualifiers` | magnitude_type from the region (the catalogue's own scale), event_id ← record:id |

## Uncertainty

Magnitude 1σ an assumed 0.2 unless the region names a column; location 1σ from the catalogue's error columns where the region names them.

## Known issues

- These catalogues were relocated with hindsight (double-difference over the whole sequence), so they only feed tasks of their own (CB-20, CB-21).
- Each computes its own local magnitude: Tan's runs ~0.26 below INGV's, Alto Tiberina's ~0.5 below, L'Aquila's ~0.1 below (median over matched quakes). The magnitude_type says ML but the scale is the catalogue's own.
- Fonzetti's relocated file (`catalog_148k_DD.csv`) has its latitude and longitude headers swapped; regions map the columns by content, not by header.
